title: SLO double-counting and rule ownership handoff notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures the on-call timeline, hypotheses, and concrete runbook/ownership changes after a week of noisy SLO burns that turned out to be caused by duplicate counting of request latencies across two pipeline exporters and a mis-routed alert group that amplified pages.

Summary of incident (high level):
- Symptom: Multiple SLO burn alerts (p99 latency and 5xx count) flared across three services between 2025-10-30 and 2025-11-03. Pager volume spiked and several pages were duplicates for the same underlying spike, creating alert fatigue.
- Impact: Brief 8–12 minute visible latency degradation for end users on the Hosted API region-us-west during peak traffic windows. No customer data loss. Increased operational load and delayed incident response.
- Root cause (short): Two exporters (legacy-prom-exporter v1 and new-kv-exporter v3) both instrumented the same request path and a recent routing change duplicated events into the exporter pipeline for ~40% of requests. Alerting rules referenced a non-deduplicated metric and an alert grouping key that differed between routes, producing separate pages for the same underlying condition.

Detailed timeline (notes from on-call):
- 2025-10-30 10:32 PDT: First p99_latency_slo_burn alert triggered for service-api-prod (pager, severity P2).
- 2025-10-30 10:35 PDT: Second p99_latency_slo_burn triggered for same service but different alert rule (latency_histogram_p99). Two separate on-call pages in parallel.
- 2025-10-30 10:37–10:45 PDT: SREs investigate. Initial hypothesis: upstream cache degradation or autoscaler lag.
- 2025-10-30 10:46 PDT: Observe number of samples in prom_histogram spike inconsistent with request volume (samples > expected req/sec * histogram_buckets).
- 2025-10-30 10:50 PDT: Correlate with exporter logs: legacy-prom-exporter shows duplicate POST payloads for some batches.
- 2025-10-30 11:06 PDT: Incident mitigated by temporary mute of one of the alert rules and throttling alerts for the service.
- 2025-10-30 11:20 PDT: Mitigation: disable legacy-prom-exporter ingestion for service-api-prod via feature-flag rollback (quick revert).

Evidence and signals used:
- Prometheus query snapshots (attached to Jira SRE-4121) showing sample count vs request count mismatch.
- Exporter logs: duplicate batch IDs visible for 40% of batches between 09:58–11:00 PDT.
- Tracing: single trace per request but two histogram observations recorded for many traces (trace_id correlated).
- Alerting history: two separate alert rules with different group_by keys both firing for the same trace window.

Root cause analysis (expanded):
1) Code/config regression: A routing change in the telemetry pipeline (PR telemetry/rel-2025-10-28) added a passthrough that caused buffered batches to be forwarded to both legacy-prom-exporter and the new-kv-exporter when a retry path executed. The retry path was hit by a small percentage of requests under certain p95 tail conditions.
2) Metric definition mismatch: The alert rules were written referencing two different metric names that both reflected the same underlying latency but aggregated independently without a deduping label (one had exporter="legacy", the other exporter omitted).
3) Alert grouping misconfiguration: Pager grouping used different grouping keys (service + region vs service + host) so the same root cause generated two pages.
4) Ownership gap: Nobody owned cross-exporter deduplication logic; both telemetry and infra teams assumed the other had validated dedupe before rollout.

Why this produced noisy SLO burns:
- Duplicate metric points artificially inflated sample counts and histogram counts, skewing the p99 calculation upward when the additional points landed in tail buckets.
- The alert rules did not include dedup labels or use a global dedup gate.
- Grouping differences created separate pages for the same burst, doubling operator attention per incident.

Immediate mitigations performed (what we did during the incident):
- Muted the lower-priority alert enumeration to reduce pages. (Pager throttle for latency_histogram_p99 for service-api-prod)
- Rolled back telemetry routing change that caused duplication (feature-flag revert).
- Set temporary silence on the legacy-prom-exporter ingestion for affected services for 2 hours while we verified data correctness.

Post-incident follow-ups and action items (owners and target dates):
- SRE / Telemetry: Implement deduplication check in the scrape pipeline that detects identical trace_id events within a 30s window. Owner: Maya Chen. ETA: 2026-02-12.
- Telemetry: Add exporter label to all latency metric families and standardize the presence/absence across all exporters. Owner: Priya Nair. ETA: 2026-01-22.
- Alerts: Modify latency SLO alert rule to use a deduped metric (or add dedupe label filter) and unify grouping key to 'service + region' to avoid split pages. Owner: Daniel Park. ETA: 2026-01-10.
- Runbook: Create an "Alerting duplication" section with quick triage steps and a checklist for temporary mute vs rollback. Owner: Jorge Alvarez. ETA: 2026-01-05.
- Product/Platform: Add a deploy-time telemetry contract checklist for any pipeline routing change (must include test of dedupe and metric identity). Owner: Eng Release PM (assign). ETA: 2026-02-01.

Runbook draft additions (quick checklist to add to SRE runbook):
- When multiple alerts for the same service fire around same timestamp:
  - Step 1: Check cardinality of metric samples vs request count (prom query snapshot). If samples >> requests, suspect duplication.
  - Step 2: Query exporter logs for duplicate batch IDs and look for identical trace_id observations.
  - Step 3: Correlate traces to confirm single trace with multiple metric observations.
  - Step 4: If duplication confirmed, temporarily mute the lower priority rule and open a rollback/feature-flag ticket against telemetry routing.
  - Step 5: Post-mortem notes: preserve all query snapshots and logs, tag Jira and Slack thread.

Suggested alert rule modifications (examples):
- Current naive rule:
  - alert: SLOLatencyP99Burn
  - expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 0.5
- Suggested guarded rule (pseudocode):
  - Replace raw metric with deduped series: deduped_latency = sum by (le, service, region) (rate(request_latency_bucket{exporter!~"legacy|duplicate"}[5m]))
  - Use grouping labels: group_by: [service, region]
  - If dedup cannot be computed in Prom: add a pre-filter exporter!~"legacy" until dedup fix is deployed.

Ownership and handoff (new policy proposal):
- Telemetry team: owns exporters, labels, and deduplication primitives. Responsible for proving non-duplication in canary before routing changes.
- Infra/SRE: owns alert rules, grouping, and runbook content. Responsible for gating pages and defining safe muting thresholds.
- Release engineering: requires a telemetry contract sign-off on deployment tickets touching the telemetry pipeline.

Verification plan (how we confirm problem is fixed):
- Metrics sanity checks for three weeks after fix: sample_count should track request_count within 3% outside of known retry windows.
- Canary test: synthetic traffic that exercises retry path should not create duplicate exporter observations in trace logs.
- Alert stability: no duplicate pages for the same incident across different rules for 30 days.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Should we prefer exporter label filtering in rules or build a dedupe aggregation in the ingestion pipeline? Tradeoffs: rules-change is faster; pipeline dedupe is cleaner long-term.
- Can we add an automated alert that detects sudden divergence between sample_count and request_count as early warning? (Probably yes — proposal attached in Jira SRE-4121).
- Who is the Release PM for the telemetry pipeline changes? Need explicit assignment to enforce the deploy-time checklist.

Notes to self / on-call learnings:
- When pages multiply, early suspicion should include telemetry duplication, not only app-layer regressions.
- Always capture the exporter label landscape snapshot as part of triage (it helps rule out simple mismatches).
- Grouping keys matter: unify them across alerts for the same SLO family to reduce operator cost.

Draft summary for Slack announcement (internal):
Hey team — quick update on the recent latency SLO burn noise: root cause was duplicated latency observations caused by a telemetry routing regression. We rolled back the change and are implementing dedup checks and alert rule hardening. Expect PRs for alert rule changes and telemetry dedupe in the next 3 weeks. Full notes: <link to Jira SRE-4121>.

Attachments and artifacts referenced (in Jira):
- prom_query_snapshots/2025-10-30/samples_vs_reqs.json
- exporter_logs/legacy-prom-exporter/2025-10-30.log
- trace_correlation/exporter-duplication-cases.csv

Action items recap (short):
- [Maya] Add dedupe detector to pipeline (ETA 2026-02-12)
- [Priya] Standardize exporter labels (ETA 2026-01-22)
- [Daniel] Update alert rules and unify grouping (ETA 2026-01-10)
- [Jorge] Update runbook with duplication triage checklist (ETA 2026-01-05)

End of notes.

Unresolved: add release PM owner and decide pipeline vs rule fix prioritization.
